audience.programmeDescription: UvA Biomedical Sciences studies how the human body works and how disease develops. The programme combines laboratory work, data analysis and independent biomedical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore disease mechanisms, population health or quantitative methods. UvA brings these areas together in a specialist biomedical curriculum.

cellNotes.text: Both introduce cell structures, biomolecules and cellular processes.
Both study human anatomy. UCR organises the material by body region and system.
Both study the functioning of human organ systems.
Both study how disease affects human organ systems.
Both study immune mechanisms. UvA includes a dedicated immunology practical.
Both examine cell structure and function and the molecular processes that regulate them.
Both study biomolecules, enzymes and metabolism.
Both develop practical molecular techniques. UCR includes DNA isolation, PCR and electrophoresis.
Both study genetic mechanisms and evolutionary change.
UvA has a dedicated microbiology survey. UCR studies selected microbes in laboratory and infection courses.
UvA studies how animals develop and function. UCR offers related study in human anatomy and physiology.
UvA teaches data science in a biomedical setting. UCR offers general programming, statistics and data analysis.
UvA teaches bioethics in a dedicated course. UCR offers broader ethical frameworks.
UvA uses microscopy to investigate biochemical processes in living cells.
UvA teaches genome analysis and the interpretation of genome-scale data.
UvA requires a short thesis on a biomedical topic.
The UvA specialisation includes a dedicated experimental genomics practical.
UvA requires an 18 EC research placement. The optional UCR research element sits outside the illustrated schedules.

notes.text: UvA combines an integrated laboratory sequence, dedicated omics study and a required research placement. The UCR options combine individual courses in biomedical science, population health or quantitative methods. Their laboratory and research experiences differ from UvA’s required sequence.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.text: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

DISDATA111.text: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.text: Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. DISDATA212.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
DISDATA212.text: Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognise structures and objects. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.

DISDATA311.text: Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python, Keras and TensorFlow implementations. Students build and train networks, study backpropagation, regularisation and model evaluation, and apply deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.

HCBBIOM313.text: Examines how normal organ-system function relates to disease.
